key_insight: Mutually incompatible martensitic states in Ti76Nb22Al2 can support a boundary-preserving microstructure through a degenerate T12 configuration, despite admitting no exact deformation with gradients restricted to those states.
engineering_relevance: The analysis links transformation-strain compatibility to observed interfaces and macroscopic shape preservation in a shape-memory alloy.
method: Apply the moving mask approximation to 12 martensitic matrices rank-one connected to austenite.
Analyze a degenerate T12 configuration under unit middle eigenvalue and volume preservation, including support on only 8 matrices.
Assess pairwise near-compatibility against observed interface frequencies.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports experimental confirmation of an identity macroscopic deformation gradient and more frequent observation of interfaces between more nearly compatible pairs.
watch_item: The existence result assumes an exactly unit middle eigenvalue and volume preservation; it does not provide an exact deformation whose gradient lies in the finite matrix set almost everywhere.
paper_title: Complex Martensitic Microstructures in ${\rm Ti}_{76}{\rm Nb}_{22}{\rm Al}_{2}$
